text:
We've got a bright, chilly late morning, with temperatures only in the low 40s and a breeze that makes it feel colder. Clouds should fill in through the afternoon, so the sun won't last. Any sprinkles up in those clouds should dry out before they reach the ground, so no umbrella needed. We still climb to around 53, with a light south wind. A jacket will do for the afternoon, and it gets dark around quarter to 6.

Tonight stays mostly clear and mild for late October, with a low around 43. The south wind picks up a bit overnight.

Thursday is the surprise. Sunshine and a gusty south wind push us to about 66, and it could get close to 70. Gusts near 28 mph will be noticeable on a walk or bike ride. A cold front brings a few showers after 8pm Thursday into the early morning, but I'd expect less than a tenth of an inch. The European model is wetter, but I'd bet on mostly dry. Friday turns breezy and cooler.

Sunny and crisp for Halloween with a high near 52, so bundle up the trick-or-treaters before a frosty night near 29.
Looks like another mostly sunny day, a touch warmer at 57, followed by a milder night in the upper 30s.
Mostly dry with a high near 57, though a stray shower is possible from the morning on as clouds build.
Looks like showers become a better bet Tuesday, day and night, with a high near 54 and clouds mixed with a little sun.

OBSERVED (2026-10-28T15:05:00+00:00): Clear, 43F feels 37F, humidity 52%, wind S 9 mph
NWS FORECAST:
  Today: Mostly cloudy, with a high near 53. South wind 6 to 9 mph.
  Tonight: Mostly clear, with a low around 43. South wind 7 to 12 mph, with gusts as high as 22 mph.
  Thursday: Sunny, with a high near 66. South wind 12 to 17 mph, with gusts as high as 28 mph.
  Thursday Night: A chance of rain showers between 8pm and 5am. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 49. Southwest wind 6 to 17 mph. Chance of precipitation is 30%. New rainfall amounts less than a tenth of an inch possible.
AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-28T10:33:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. A brief spike in temperatures is expected for Thursday, which will return closer to normal after a cold front mostly notable for the breezy conditions it will bring.
  2. Dry and seasonable weather is expected over the weekend, with chances for showers returning next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 223 AM EDT Wednesday... No notable changes have been made to the forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Despite the dewpoint depressions, light winds, clear skies, and surface high pressure, the radiational cooling has not been very pronounced. There's still some time before high clouds and warm advection begin, but it seems we'll not fall as low as forecast. Temperatures are still plenty cool with 20s across the region. A compact vort will track northeast. Clouds will overspread the region much of the day, and there should be some signs of virga. A very dry layer from the surface-850mb will likely prevent any precipitation from reaching the ground. Forecast soundings suggest precipitation should make it to about 5000-6000 ft elevation before evaporating/sublimating away. Overall, a somewhat dreary, but not a bad weather day as temperatures climb into the 50s with light south winds. Tonight into Thursday, those south winds will increase ahead of an incoming frontal boundary. South winds overnight will mean that the Champlain Valley and northern slopes of the Adirondacks will be warmest with low to mid 40s, while the rest of the region should still fall in and around the freezing mark. The same areas will likely also observe the strongest gusts by mid afternoon, likely ranging from 25-35 mph. Temperatures will respond with the steady south to southwest winds, and climb into the 60s, perhaps even touching 70 F. NBM probabilities range 10-50%, and the forecast expressly has 70 F for areas like Fort Covington, Mooers, and Altona, New York. For the front, there are no significant changes. A modest frontal boundary will shift southeast. Recent dryness will make its narrow moisture feed unlikely to produce significant precipitation as synoptic support falters, and the frontal boundary stretches out. So there will be a northwest-southeast "gradient" where northern areas receive a few hundredths, and areas to the south receive little to no precipitation. More seasonable temperatures into the 50s in the day and 20s-lower 30s at night return behind the front. Postfrontal gusts will be strongest on Friday with good afternoon mixing bringing gusty northwest winds of 20-30 mph, locally to 35 mph for areas like Ellenburg, NY. KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure will build over the region for the weekend, bringing another period of dry and seasonable weather. High temperatures will generally climb into the 50s and low 60s this weekend. Heading into next week, it looks there could be a few chances for showers towards the start of next week, although some of the latest global deterministic models suggest the dry pattern we've been in will continue into early next week. We'll have to keep and eye on trends given the large amount of uncertainty at this stage.
PLAIN-WORDS BRIEF (rules from the same NWS data, already on the page): Mostly cloudy today, high 53. Mostly clear tonight, low 43. Thursday, sunny and warmer, high 66.
LAKE GAGE: water 52F, level 93.98 ft (normal)

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - It was a chilly start to our Wednesday morning with most waking up to temperatures in the teens and 20s. More cloud cover begins to fill in through the morning hours today leaving us gray and cloudier into this afternoon. Temperatures are a tad warmer though, as we climb towards the upper 40s and 50s for afternoon highs. Thursday we look to be even warmer as most climb towards the low and even mid-60s for Thursday afternoon. A few clouds may begin to build in through the day Thursday and could give way to a few showers Thursday evening into Thursday night. Any rain should be wrapping up by Friday morning, but we may hang onto a bit more cloud cover through the day Friday with high temperatures in the upper 50s to lower 60s. The weekend forecast at this point is not looking too bad. Saturday for Halloween features nice sunshine with temperatures in the 50s. Trick-or-treat time remains clear as temperatures dip into the 40s. Don’t forget we fall back 1 hour Saturday night into Sunday. Sunday features more sunshine with high temperatures in the 50s. There is a chance for maybe a few hit-or-miss showers into Monday with temperatures again in the 50s to about 60° for Monday afternoon. There is a chance for a spotty shower or two, but most will likely stay dry. Tuesday again features more clouds and a chance for a spotty shower with high temperatures in the 50s to about 60°.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-27T22:07:00Z — same caveat): Mostly cloudy, but turning a bit milder Wednesday — Wednesday will feature a mostly cloudy sky, with a few more breaks of sun likely by afternoon. It turns a bit milder — highs rebound to the low and mid-50s. Thursday turns warmer, as a gusty south breeze sends highs to around 70. Expect lots of sunshine through the morning and afternoon. A cold front brings a band of clouds and spotty showers during the evening, lasting into the overnight. Friday turns mostly dry, with only a spot shower leftover. However, expect more clouds than sun with highs falling back to the 50s. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs in the upper 40s. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the mid-50s, as sun mixes with clouds. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday looks brightest, then more clouds and a greater chance for showers arrive by mid to late week.
